text: {"memo": "Tesla delivered modest top‑line growth in FY2024, with revenue reaching $97.69\u202fbillion versus $96.77\u202fbillion in FY2023. However, profitability eroded sharply: net income fell to $7.09\u202fbillion from $15.00\u202fbillion a year earlier, and operating income slipped to $7.08\u202fbillion from $8.89\u202fbillion. The decline was reflected in diluted EPS, which dropped to $2.04 per share in FY2024 from $4.30 in FY2023. Operating cash flow improved, rising to $14.92\u202fbillion in FY2024 from $13.26\u202fbillion in FY2023. Margins contracted notably: net margin fell to roughly 7% in FY2024 from about 15% in FY2023, while operating margin slipped to around 7% from roughly 9% a year ago. The mixed results suggest Tesla is navigating a transition period, balancing incremental revenue gains with significant pressure on earnings and profitability. One‑line view: TSLA remains a high‑conviction growth story but warrants caution amid declining margins and earnings."}
